rapport_notes: Warm, conversational tone with frequent validation ('yeah, that makes more sense'), good active listening, and genuine engagement with the customer's concerns.
process_discipline_notes: Rep did not hold silence after open-ended questions; frequently filled space with 'Mm-hmm' and immediate re-explanations rather than waiting for the customer to fully process or respond.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'Do you have a few minutes to just run through some details with me? Okay, perfect so before I kind of dive into deep' — frames the ask but does not time-box it or explicitly promise an accurate quote in return.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Chauny: 'before I kind of dive into deep, do you have any like, top of my concerns or questions that I can just kind of answer right out the gate?' — Asked before logistics probing begins.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about time estimate (4h 44min seems high for a short move). Rep responds with explanation but does not probe deeper: 'So it depends so Emma is the one which is our system... she kinda spits out an estimate now generally she's like on track.' Rep pivots immediately to logistics (unit number, parking) rather than asking 'What specifically worries you about the timing?' or 'Is there a time window that would work better for you?' One-layer acknowledge-and-pivot pattern.
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Not asked or answered anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Not asked or answered anywhere in the call.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep says 'I typically a one bedroom apartment honestly takes about two and a half to three and a half is what we'd like to arrange that. So which is our minimum so it generally takes around our minimum which is two and a half hours' — gives a range (2.5–3.5 hrs) but does not personalize beyond 'you're on the fifth floor' reference. Does not anchor to typical movers/hours in a structured way (e.g., 'a typical 1BR takes 2 movers 2.5–4 hours, and since you're on a higher floor with walks, I'd expect you toward the higher end').
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: Rep states 'you only pay for the time you use anyway. So while the estimate may be saying, you know, it's about three to four hours. If it does end up being the two and a half to three. That's all you end up paying for anyway' — covers the 'window' concept and reinforces it later ('you only pay for the time you use').
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Covered. Rep: 'you only pay for the time you use anyway... If it does end up being the two and a half to three. That's all you end up paying for anyway.'
evidence_quotes.self_prep_tip: Covered. Rep: 'how well prepared you are when we get there if we're just wrapping and pad and furniture obviously that's gonna help on the time. So that way it can kind of counter act the access things that we have to go through.'
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_then_silence: Rep asks 'Does that make sense?' but does not wait for silence; immediately continues with 'So yeah, so, I wouldn't really worry too much about the estimate...' No held silence after the open question.
evidence_quotes.close: Call ends with 'Okay, beautiful. Well you have an amazing rest of your weekend and we will see you on the twentieth.' No rate-lock statement, no explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?'). Confirmation email is mentioned but no direct close line.

top_strength: Chauny expertly pivoted the customer's pricing concern by personalizing the estimate through logistics discovery (floors, elevator walks, parking) and reframed the issue as time-of-use rather than a fixed estimate, defusing objection with clarity and transparency.
coaching_note: Never asked about careful handling of items or who the customer will meet (Meet Your Mover), and failed to deliver the Stage 2 takeaway (On-Time Guarantee and Communication differentiators); additionally, hold silence after open-ended questions rather than immediately filling the space with validation or re-explanation.
